title: Declarative tool-binding orchestration shim and validator for SDKs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
Build a language-agnostic orchestration shim and declarative validator for 'tool' (function) bindings in our SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). The goal is a single extensible contract that SDKs can use to: 1) validate developer-provided tool schemas before runtime, 2) normalize invocation payloads across languages, 3) provide a unified streaming + retry ergonomic surface for tool invocation, and 4) emit structured telemetry for debugging and cost attribution.

Goals:
- Provide a declarative JSON/Type schema format (backwards-compatible with existing function schemas) and a small semantics layer describing: required/optional params, coercion rules, streaming vs non-streaming, and idempotency markers for safe retries.
- Implement per-SDK lightweight validators that run at call-site (dev experience) and again as a runtime guard in the request pipeline.
- Add an invocation shim that: chooses best retry strategy based on idempotency + latency SLO, unwraps streaming responses into language-native iterators/async generators, and supports a graceful fallback path when a tool is unavailable (model fallback or direct model call).
- Provide examples and tests for: nested object coercion, enum normalization, streaming binary payloads, function version pinning, and cross-language behavior parity.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not the full rollout for server-side model routing or Dedicated-only auth changes. It focuses on SDK helpers and client-side validation/orchestration.

Design decisions and trade-offs (high level):
- Declarative format: JSON Schema-lite (small subset) to balance expressiveness and implementability across languages. Full JSON Schema is powerful but heavy; we'll restrict to types, enums, required lists, coercion hints, and an "x-idempotent" boolean.
- Two-phase validation: cheaper client-side checks at development time (fast fail/IDE feedback) and a stricter runtime guard in the outbound request pipeline (defense in depth).
- Retries: default to exponential backoff + jitter for transient network errors; only auto-retry when x-idempotent=true. For streaming responses, retries are not transparent; the shim will expose a resumable cursor API in Python/TS and an explicit resume token in Go.

API sketches (examples):
- Python (sync/async):
  from redwood_sdk.tools import bind_tool, ToolSchemaError

  my_schema = {
    "name": "lookup_customer",
    "params": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "required": true}},
    "x-idempotent": true
  }

  tool = bind_tool(my_schema, handler=my_local_handler)

  # streaming call as async generator
  async for chunk in client.call_tool_stream(tool, {"customer_id": "123"}):
      handle(chunk)

- TypeScript (promise + async iterator):
  import {bindTool, callTool} from '@redwood/sdk'

  const tool = bindTool(schema)
  for await (const chunk of callTool.stream(tool, {id: '123'})) { console.log(chunk) }

- Go (explicit resume token):
  schema := loadSchema(bytes)
  tool := bindTool(schema)
  resp, err := client.CallTool(context, tool, params)
  if resp.Streaming { // resp.ResumeToken available }

Acceptance criteria:
- Client-side validators implemented for Python, TS, and Go that catch at least 90% of common schema mistakes in our integration tests.
- Orchestration shim exposes identical high-level behavior (streaming iterator/resume semantics and retry policy) across languages.
- Unit + integration tests covering schema coercions, idempotency gating of retries, and fallback path when tool handler returns 503.
- Docs + sample repo updated (examples for each language).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (this ticket): implement validators + shim + unit tests and examples. PR linked below.
- Stage 2: dogfood with Redwood Console end-to-end example, measure mis-binding errors and latency impact.
- Stage 3: enable server-side runtime guard for Hosted API as a config flag (follow-up ticket).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Tool+Binding+Design
- Draft design slides: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1t6B-example
- Initial PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1284
- Example app (python + ts): https://github.com/redwood-inference/tooling-examples/tree/eng-74290

Deployment/observability notes:
- Emit telemetry events: tool.bind.success/fail, tool.call.start/complete/error, tool.stream.resume. Ensure traces include schema version and x-idempotent metadata.
- Add unit-level cost tagging so tool invocations are visible in Console token-level breakdown.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Server-side enforcement ticket to add full runtime guard + schema migration helper.
- UX: add schema validation warnings in Console and a schema linter extension for VSCode/TS.
